newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Merko targets $55 million turnover in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turk Merko targets $55 million turnover in 1997.

text.p: Turkish canned and frozen food and vegetables producers Merko Gida Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. and Konfrut Gida Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. aim to increase their sales turnover sharply this year, a senior company official said.

"Our capacities are enough to realise $55 million (63 trillio lira) turnover in Merko and $28 million (3.2 trillion lira) in Konfrut in 1997," Hakan Severge, the general manager of the companies, told Reuters. Merko and Konfrut are owned by the same group, known as Merko group.

Merko reported 2.5 trillion lira of turnover in the first nine months of 1996, against 1.1 trillion lira in the same period of 1995. Net profit of the company rose to 324 billion lira in the first nine months of 1996 from 150 billion lira in 1995.
Konfrut reported 1.1 trillion lira turnover and 200 billion lira net profit in the first nine months of 1996, up from 492.9 billion and 50.8 billion lira in the same 1995 period, respectively.
Severge said they achieved their 1996 targets of sales and profits in both companies.
"In 1996 we could not reach our export targets, because of the Polish and Hungarian competition in the European market and the recession in Germany" he said.
"But we offset the gap by exceeding our targets for tomato paste sales," he added.
Merko shares, listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange, opened at 6,700 lira on Monday, against 6,500 lira of Friday's close and Konfrut at 17,750 lira against 17,500 lira on Friday.
Severge said they would increase the tomato paste production capacity by 100 percent in 1997, thanks to an investment of $4.5 million to meet the market demand.
"We do not want to make any further investments in 1997. We want a gradual growth instead of a rapid growth," he said, adding that the group aimed at keeping the growth rate below 25 percent.
Severge said they aimed to increase the total exports of both companies to $40 million in 1997 from $32.5 million in 1996.
